promises.quote: I have set out below more detailed information on how health and safety incidents are regulated in the health and adult social care sectors in England and on regulatory responsibility in respect of medical devices.
promises.summary: HSE will not address anti-choking device concerns; refer to CQC and MHRA.

concerns.quote: there is not wide knowledge of the availability of these devices in care settings and if more homes had them it is likely that deaths from choking could be reduced

concerns.quote: restaurants have first aid items and some may have equipment such as a defibrillator however they may not be aware that this useful item exists, nor that it is relatively inexpensive
concerns.hazard: lack of awareness of choking assistance devices in restaurants

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of awareness about the availability and usefulness of anti‑choking devices in specific settings. The earlier report concerns care homes, while the later report concerns restaurants and food establishments.
links.earlier_quote: [REDACTED], who has considerable experience working in health and social care, said she was concerned that there was not wider knowledge of the existence of these devices particularly for homes that have a high volume of residents with choking risks like Acorn Care Home.
links.later_quote: During the evidence it was heard that there is a device that may assist in incidents of choking, it was referred to as a LifeVac (this may be a trade name).
